data.title: US court rules Pentagon ban of Anthropic unlawful
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - A US federal judge ruled on Thursday that sanctions imposed by the Trump administration against AI giant Anthropic were illegal, finding that the government punished the company in a row over military use of its technology.

data.title: Anger in Austria over business park on former Nazi camp site
data.description: LEOBERSDORF (AUSTRIA) - A few crumbling concrete blocks in an overgrown field are all that remains visible of what was once a sprawling Nazi forced labour complex around the Austrian town of Leobersdorf.

data.title: Tanker pays record US$5.3 mn to transit Panama Canal: administrator
data.description: PANAMA CITY - A tanker carrying liquefied petroleum gas has paid US$5.3 million (175 million baht) for priority passage through the Panama Canal ahead of El Nino-related restrictions, the waterway's deputy administrator, Ilya Espino de Marotta, told AFP on Thursday.

data.title: Fresh flood warnings for disaster-hit Nepal and Tibet, 1,400 still missing
data.description: BIDUR (NEPAL) - China and Nepal warned of fresh flooding risks, complicating rescuers' search Friday for more than 1,400 people missing after a deadly deluge and landslides swept away entire villages along their remote Himalayan border.

data.title: Pilgrims seeking peace caught in deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
data.description: BIDUR (NEPAL) - They came to the Himalayas seeking spiritual renewal, drawn by Tibet's sacred, snow-capped Mount Kailash.

data.title: US court rules Pentagon ban of Anthropic unlawful
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - A US federal judge ruled on Thursday that sanctions imposed in February by the Trump administration against AI giant Anthropic were illegal, finding that the government had punished the artificial intelligence company for publicly criticising the Pentagon.

data.title: Why Filipino migrants are rethinking their futures in Japan
data.description: MANILA — When Japan’s embassy in the Philippines extended applications for healthcare jobs on April 15, the pitch was straightforward: 50 positions for nurses and 300 for care workers in Japan, a three- to four-year placement, free Japanese-language lessons in both countries and a daily allowance during training.

data.title: Most Asian stocks advance as attention turns to Warsh speech
data.description: HONG KONG - Asian stocks mostly rose on Friday ahead of a closely watched speech by Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh that investors will be parsing for clues about the outlook for interest rates amid elevated inflation and no sign of an end to the Middle East crisis.

data.title: China's help critical, but unlikely, for US to choke off Iran
data.description: BEIJING - The United States has threatened the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, but analysts say that a successful chokehold would require unlikely cooperation from China.

data.title: In Zambia, a Shaolin Temple offers a softer face of China
data.description: NGWERERE (ZAMBIA) - From a distance, the Shaolin Temple outside Lusaka appeared almost like a mirage, a slice of central China dropped into the Zambian landscape.

data.title: Air traffic controllers left early before deadly NY crash
data.description: NEW YORK - Two air traffic controllers left work early ahead of a deadly collision between an Air Canada jet and a fire truck at New York's LaGuardia Airport in March, The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.

data.title: Corals show El Nino intensifying as planet warms: study
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Coral skeleton records stretching back 1,000 years show El Nino episodes are intensifying as the planet warms, carrying major implications for a future under climate change, according to a new study Thursday.

data.title: Trump says Russia is 'not going to attack' NATO territory
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump on Thursday said Vladimir Putin is "not going to attack" NATO territory, pushing back against media reports that Washington is concerned about a possible Russian move on Europe.

data.title: Russia dismisses as 'scare stories' US reports about attacking NATO
data.description: MOSCOW - The Kremlin on Thursday dismissed as "scare stories" US media reports suggesting that Russia could attack NATO, following a rare visit by the CIA director to Moscow.

data.title: Iran executes over 500 people in 2026: rights group
data.description: PARIS — Iran has executed over 500 people so far this year after a new surge in hangings in recent days, despite United States President Donald Trump urging the Islamic republic to halt executions, a rights group said on Thursday.

data.title: Zambia opposition leader surrenders to police: state media
data.description: LUSAKA - The Zambian opposition leader who was runner-up in this month's disputed presidential election surrendered to police on Thursday after two weeks in hiding following a summons over an alleged national security threat, state media reported.

data.title: Srebrenica: Massacre that outraged the world
data.description: SARAJEVO - Srebrenica became a symbol of ethnic cleansing after its men and boys were massacred by Bosnian Serbs following a three-year-long siege during the Balkan wars of the 1990s.

data.title: Alleged 9/11 mastermind to go on trial in June 2028
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the alleged mastermind of the September 11, 2001 attacks on the United States, will go on trial before a US military court in June 2028, an official said Thursday.

data.title: After US settlement, EU says Meta must 'protect our kids too'
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - The EU said Thursday it expects Meta to address "addictive" features of its platforms in Europe, after the tech giant agreed to sweeping limits on teen use of Facebook and Instagram in some US states.

data.title: 'Butcher of Bosnia' Ratko Mladic dead: Serbian state media
data.description: THE HAGUE - ⁠Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb military chief dubbed the "Butcher of Bosnia" for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, has died, Serbian state broadcaster RTS reported on Thursday.

data.title: Iran, Qatar hold Hormuz talks as US blockade chokes Iran oil imports
data.description: TEHRAN - Iran's top diplomat met his Qatari counterpart on Thursday in Tehran for talks on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, as a US naval blockade squeezes oil supplies to Iran amid a domestic shortfall.

data.title: Swallowed by silt: Survivors recount Nepal flood horror
data.description: BIDUR (NEPAL) - Survivors from Nepal's flood-ravaged districts, some on stretchers, others supported by the shoulders, being airlifted to safety on Thursday from the town of Bidur, spoke of the devastation that hit their community.

data.title: Devastation of Pakistan infant ward fire revealed
data.description: ISLAMABAD - Twisted ceiling frames, charred walls and a shaft of sunlight piercing a partially collapsed roof were all that was left of a neonatal ward on Thursday after a devastating hospital fire killed 14 infants in Pakistan.

data.title: Germany reports record 15,800 heat-related deaths
data.description: BERLIN - Germany has registered a record 15,800 heat-related deaths this summer as Europe struggles through a series of punishing heatwaves, the national public health institute said Thursday.

data.title: Activists stand up to fellow Jews to protect Palestinians
data.description: JANNATAH, Palestinian Territories - Ziva Sharp said her Jewish faith motivated her to travel from Jerusalem to the West Bank to stand up for Palestinians — a commitment that led to her being set upon by fellow Israelis also professing to be driven by Judaism.

data.title: Taiwan approves $7.6bn drone budget as China threat grows
data.description: TAIPEI - Lawmakers in Taiwan approved a US$7.6-billion budget for locally made drones on Thursday as the island democracy seeks to strengthen its defences against a potential Chinese attack.

data.title: Norway’s King Harald in ‘extremely serious’ condition
data.description: OSLO - The health of Norway’s 89-year-old King Harald, hospitalised with a blood disease, has deteriorated and he is in an “extremely serious” condition, the palace said Thursday.

data.title: Desperate families search for missing after Nepal floods
data.description: KATHMANDU (NEPAL) - Anxious relatives crowded the corridors of a Kathmandu hospital Thursday as they searched for missing family after devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 165 people.

data.title: Political intrigue in Uganda as succession battle heats up
data.description: NAIROBI - Uganda’s tempestuous army chief has once again vowed to run for president and succeed his long-ruling father, but palace intrigues are swirling as he faces a challenge from a brother-in-law.

data.title: Thai caught smuggling parrot eggs in South Africa
data.description: South African customs officials have arrested a Thai national trying to smuggle 50 endangered parrot eggs, some of which have since hatched, through Johannesburg’s main airport.

data.title: Climate change leaves mark on America’s largest reservoir
data.description: LAKE MEAD, Nevada - From high in the hills around Las Vegas, tourist Choune Osterero gazes down at the line of chalky mineral deposits left on the rocks around Lake Mead as the level of America’s largest reservoir has dropped over the last quarter of a century of drought.

data.title: Nepal-Tibet disaster: what we know

data.title: China deploys record number of ships around Taiwan
data.description: TAIPEI - China deployed a record number of coast guard, scientific research and other ships in Taiwan’s waters last month, the island’s coast guard told AFP, as Beijing dials up pressure on Taipei.

data.title: CIA head ‘warned Russia not to attack NATO members’
data.description: WASHINGTON - A highly unusual trip by the CIA director to Moscow this week was to warn Russia against any attack on NATO member states, US media reported Wednesday, after President Donald Trump sought to downplay the visit.
